parole.significato: A traditional Galician unit of dry measure, equivalent to about 1–1.5 L depending on the substance measured.
parole.testo: From Galician cunca (“bowl, ¹⁄₆₀ Galician bushel”), from Old Galician-Portuguese cunca, from Latin concha (“mussel, vessel”), from Ancient Greek κόγχη (kónkhē, “shell, mussel”).

parole.significato: A traditional Galician unit of dry measure, equivalent to about 6–9 L depending on the substance measured.
parole.testo: From Galician escá, from Hispanic Late Latin scala (“bowl”) attested in Isidore of Seville, probably from Suevic, from Proto-Germanic *skēlō (“bowl”). Cognate with German Schale and Dutch schaal.

parole.significato: A traditional Galician unit of dry measure, equivalent to about 12–18 L depending on the substance measured.
parole.testo: From Galician ferrado, from Medieval Latin modius ferrātus (“reinforced modius”), from Latin ferrātus (“ironed”), from ferrum (“iron”) + -ātus (“-ate”).
